explanation.body: The rated values give $R_X=10^2/20=5.0\ \Omega$ and $R_Y=5^2/2=12.5\ \Omega$. The series voltage divider gives $V_X=15.0(5.0)/(12.5+5.0)=4.3\ \mathrm V$ and $V_Y=15.0(12.5)/(12.5+5.0)=10.7\ \mathrm V$. Using $P=V^2/R$ with these resistances, X dissipates less than $20\ \mathrm W$ and Y dissipates more than $2\ \mathrm W$.

perOption.A: Assumes each bulb receives its rated voltage.
perOption.B: Reverses which bulb is above its rated voltage.
perOption.C: Correct. X is below its rated power and Y is above its rated power.
perOption.D: Treats Y as underpowered even though its p.d. exceeds 5 V.

difficultyReason: Requires finding the lamp resistances from their ratings and applying the voltage divider.

transcription:
Two bulbs are connected in series to a $15\ \mathrm V$ power supply. Bulb X is rated $10\ \mathrm V$, $20\ \mathrm W$ and Bulb Y is rated $5\ \mathrm V$, $2\ \mathrm W$.

[One series loop contains the $15\ \mathrm V$ supply, an open switch and bulbs X and Y.]

Which of the following best describes the power output of the bulbs when the switch is closed?

Power output of bulb X | Power output of bulb Y
A. $20\ \mathrm W$ | $2\ \mathrm W$
B. greater than $20\ \mathrm W$ | smaller than $2\ \mathrm W$
C. smaller than $20\ \mathrm W$ | greater than $2\ \mathrm W$
D. smaller than $20\ \mathrm W$ | smaller than $2\ \mathrm W$

explanation.body: The resistance is $R=\rho l/A$, and the volume $lA$ is constant. Hence $R=\rho l^2/(lA)$ is proportional to $l^2$, so the graph rises with an increasing gradient.

perOption.A: Correct. The resistance is proportional to the square of the length.
perOption.B: Treats cross-sectional area as fixed, giving a linear increase.
perOption.C: Confuses constant volume with constant resistance.
perOption.D: Predicts a decrease although the longer wire is also thinner.

difficultyReason: Requires substituting the fixed-volume constraint before selecting a graph.
misconception: Holding cross-sectional area constant across wires

explanation.body: Use the right-hand grip rule for each wire. At O the fields from P and R point up and left, while those from Q and S point up and right. The fields have equal magnitudes, so the horizontal components cancel and the vertical components add upwards.

perOption.A: Correct. All four vertical components point upwards.
perOption.B: Keeps a rightward component that is cancelled by equal leftward components.
perOption.C: Reverses the vertical directions found with the grip rule.
perOption.D: Keeps a leftward component that is cancelled by equal rightward components.

difficultyReason: Requires applying the grip rule four times and adding the field components.
misconception: Taking the field to point along the line to the wire
transcription:
Four parallel straight wires carrying equal currents pass through four corners of a square PQRS as shown below. The currents in wires P and Q are directed out of the page and the currents in wires R and S are directed into the page.

Which one of the options gives the direction of the resultant magnetic field at O?

[Square with Q at top left, R at top right, P at bottom left and S at bottom right. O is the centre. The option arrows from O are A upwards, B rightwards, C downwards and D leftwards.]

explanation.body: A high steady direct current in X produces a large, constant flux linkage in Y. With no change in flux linkage, there is no induced e.m.f. and the voltmeter gives no reading.

perOption.A: A rapid increase in current changes Y's flux linkage and induces an e.m.f.
perOption.B: Even a slow decrease changes Y's flux linkage and induces an e.m.f.
perOption.C: An alternating current changes Y's flux linkage even at low amplitude.
perOption.D: Correct. A steady direct current gives constant flux linkage.

difficultyReason: Requires distinguishing steady magnetic flux linkage from changing linkage.
misconception: Assuming a large steady flux induces an e.m.f.

explanation.body: Loops 3 and 4 have constant magnetic flux linkage, so neither has an induced e.m.f., induced current or magnetic force. Loop 2 loses outward flux, so by Lenz’s law it carries an anticlockwise induced current and Fleming’s left-hand rule gives a downward force. Loop 1 gains outward flux, so its induced current is clockwise and the force is upwards.

perOption.A: Includes loop 2, whose induced current produces a downward force.
perOption.B: Assigns an upward force to loop 2 as it leaves the field.
perOption.C: Correct. Only loop 1 experiences an upward force.
perOption.D: Assumes motion within a uniform field changes flux linkage through the loops.

issues: The key’s final parenthetical says loop 2 where the upward force refers to loop 1.
difficultyReason: Requires tracking flux changes and converting the resulting induced currents into force directions.
misconception: Assuming any loop moving in a magnetic field experiences a net force

explanation.body: When the upper diode is forward-biased, the total resistance is $1\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$, so the peak current is $V_{\mathrm{peak}}/(1\ \mathrm{k}\Omega)$. In the other half-cycle the diode in series with the $5\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$ resistor conducts, so the total resistance is $6\ \mathrm{k}\Omega$. Its peak current is $V_{\mathrm{peak}}/(6\ \mathrm{k}\Omega)$, smaller and in the opposite direction.

perOption.A: Treats both conducting paths as having equal resistance.
perOption.B: Correct. The opposite-direction half-cycle has a smaller peak magnitude.
perOption.C: Ignores the current through the lower branch in the reverse half-cycle.
perOption.D: Shows both half-cycles flowing in the same direction.

difficultyReason: Requires tracing conduction separately in both halves of the a.c. cycle.
misconception: Assuming antiparallel diodes give equal or same-direction currents

explanation.body: The shortest wavelength is $0.02\ \mathrm{nm}$, so the largest photon energy is $E=hc/\lambda=(6.63\times10^{-34})(3\times10^8)/(0.02\times10^{-9})=9.945\times10^{-15}\ \mathrm J$. The electron must gain this energy from the accelerating field, so $(1.6\times10^{-19})V=9.945\times10^{-15}$ and $V\approx62\,000\ \mathrm V$.

perOption.D: Correct. The shortest wavelength sets the minimum accelerating voltage.

transcription:
When a nucleus of uranium-235 absorbs a neutron in a nuclear reactor, it undergoes fission to form various products and releases further neutrons.

In one nuclear reaction involving the fission of uranium-235, barium-144 and another element, Z, are the products. Two neutrons are also released when these products are formed. The reaction is shown in the equation.

$^{235}_{92}\mathrm U+n\to{}^{144}_{56}\mathrm{Ba}+Z+2n$

How many neutrons are there in the nucleus of Z?

A. 53
B. 54
C. 90
D. 91

explanation.body: A $10\ \mathrm g$ sample of living wood would have a count rate of $200$ per minute. The count rate halves from $200$ to $100$ and then to $50$ per minute, so the age is two half-lives, or $2(5600)=11\,200$ years.

perOption.B: Uses half a half-life even though the count rate has halved twice.

5  C

The weights $W_1$ and $W_2$ provide the tension forces, balancing the weight of the object in equilibrium. Drawing a vector triangle of proportional magnitudes:

[Two strings pass over rods at left and right and meet at a junction supporting an object of weight $10\ \mathrm N$. The hanging weights are $W_1$ at left and $W_2$ at right. The angle between the sloping strings is $\theta$, and they make angles $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ with the horizontal. The force triangle has a downward $10\ \mathrm N$ side, a $6.0\ \mathrm N$ side pointing up and left and an $8.0\ \mathrm N$ side pointing up and right.]

Recognize it is a 6-8-10 right-angled triangle. (similar to a 3-4-5).

Analysing the horizontal components in equilibrium:
$6.0\cos\theta_1=8.0\cos\theta_2\Rightarrow\theta_1<\theta_2$

Thus, $W_1=6.0\ \mathrm N$, $W_2=8.0\ \mathrm N$
